tools.name: list_brands
tools.description: List the brands (websites) tracked in this Howseen account, with their id, name and domain. Call this first when the account may have several brands.

tools.name: get_visibility
tools.description: Headline AI visibility of a brand: % of AI answers that name it, share of voice vs competitors, average position, sentiment, per engine, plus the trend over the period (one point per scan).

tools.name: list_prompts
tools.description: The buyer questions (prompts) tracked for a brand, with per-prompt visibility, share of voice, position, which engines name the brand, and which brands and domains are cited.

tools.name: get_competitors
tools.description: Compare the brand with its competitors in AI answers: visibility %, share of voice, average position and sentiment, overall and per engine.

tools.name: get_top_sources
tools.description: The domains and URLs AI engines cite most when answering the brand's buyer questions, overall and per engine. Use it to find where the brand should get listed or mentioned.

tools.name: search_responses
tools.description: Read real AI answers collected for the brand: excerpts around the brand mention, whether the brand and which competitors were named, and the cited URLs. Filter by a word in the question or answer (query), by prompt text, and by engine.

tools.name: get_action_plan
tools.description: Prioritized actions to raise the brand's AI visibility (off-page: get listed on the pages AI cites; content: answer uncovered buyer questions), ranked 20/80 like the dashboard Action plan, with steps.

tools.name: list_articles
tools.description: Articles Howseen wrote for the brand (drafts, scheduled and published), with status, target question, GEO score and published URL.

tools.name: get_prompt_gaps
tools.description: Tracked prompts where AI names at least one competitor but not the brand, per engine, with the competitors named and the domains cited. Sorted by search volume (when a cached figure exists) then by number of competitors named. Start here to see what to win back.

tools.name: get_easiest_wins
tools.description: Third-party sites and pages cited in the answers the brand loses (competitor named, brand not), ranked by how many lost answers cite them, with the matching action-plan item. Getting listed there is the shortest path back into those answers.

tools.name: get_changes
tools.description: What changed between the last two completed scans (or since a date): prompts gained and lost, visibility delta per engine, tracked competitors newly named, and the likely causes (sources that started or stopped citing the brand).

tools.name: suggest_prompts
tools.description: Buyer questions worth tracking that the brand does not track yet: real questions from Hacker News discussions (ranked by engagement) plus AI suggestions for the category. Returns suggestions only; use add_prompts to track some. Limited to 20 calls per day.

tools.name: get_article_performance
tools.description: Articles written for the brand with status, GEO score, published URL and search-engine indexing status (Google URL Inspection, Bing), plus impressions and clicks when Search Console or Bing is connected.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Plan, quotas used and left (prompts, competitors, articles, manual scans), next automatic scan estimate, what this API key may do, and the API rate limits. Call it before planning changes.

tools.name: mark_action_done
tools.description: Mark an action-plan item as done (same state as the dashboard Action plan). Use the action id from get_action_plan or get_easiest_wins. Preview first; confirm: true applies.

tools.name: dismiss_action
tools.description: Dismiss an action-plan item the user does not want to do (moves it to Archived in the dashboard, out of the next best actions). Reversible in the dashboard. Preview first; confirm: true applies.

tools.name: add_prompts
tools.description: Track new buyer questions (prompts) for the brand, checked against the plan's prompt quota (the whole list is refused if it would exceed it). An archived prompt added again is restored. Preview first; confirm: true applies.

tools.name: remove_prompts
tools.description: Stop tracking prompts and remove them from the prompt list (past scan results stay in history). Prefer archive_prompts to keep them listed. Preview first; confirm: true applies.

tools.name: archive_prompts
tools.description: Archive prompts: they stop being scanned (frees prompt quota) but keep their history and stay listed as archived in the dashboard, restorable. Preview first; confirm: true applies.

tools.name: add_competitor
tools.description: Track a competitor from a name or a website URL (resolved to name + domain like in Settings), within the competitor quota. Preview first; confirm: true applies.

tools.name: remove_competitor
tools.description: Stop tracking a competitor (by name or domain). Past results keep it. Preview first; confirm: true applies.

tools.name: draft_article
tools.description: Write a DRAFT article answering one buyer question, with the same quality pipeline as the app (brand context, sources AI cites, GEO checks). Never publishes. Uses the plan's article allowance. Preview first; confirm: true writes it (up to about a minute).

tools.name: refresh_article
tools.description: Rewrite a WRITTEN article with the brand's current profile (offer, category, offerings, competitors) after it changed: same article id, slug, question and date, previous version kept (restorable in the app). A published article is never overwritten: the update lands in a refreshed draft. Free once p

tools.name: create_share_report
tools.description: Create a public, frozen report link (visibility, competitors, top prompts, recommendations) with the account's agency branding, like the dashboard Share button. Preview first; confirm: true creates the link.

tools.name: run_scan
tools.description: Scan the brand's prompts on the AI engines now, with the same limit as the dashboard Run now button (a fresh scan at most once per brand per plan cadence: every 72h, every 24h on Business; prompts added since the last scan can be scanned alone; an unfinished scan can be continued). Preview first; co

tools.name: publish_article
tools.description: Publish a written article (e.g. a draft from draft_article) to the brand's connected CMS (WordPress, Shopify, Ghost, BigCommerce, GoHighLevel, Webflow, webhook) or hosted blog, now, or schedule it for a later date (needs Autopilot ON). Goes live publicly. Preview first; confirm: true publishes and r

tools.name: request_indexing
tools.description: Submit a published article to the search engines connected for the brand: Google (sitemap re-submit through Search Console when connected with indexing), Bing (Webmaster key) or IndexNow for pages hosted by Howseen. If you publish on your own site from the API or feed, pass url (the live https addre

tools.name: delete_article
tools.description: Move an article (planned, draft or published) to the Trash, like the dashboard delete button: restorable with restore_article or in Howseen > Content > Trash, and its topic is not planned again. A post already live on the client's own CMS (WordPress, Shopify...) is NOT removed from the CMS: the prev

tools.name: restore_article
tools.description: Bring back an article from the Trash (e.g. one deleted with delete_article). Preview first; confirm: true restores.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_top_sources, search_responses, list_articles, get_article_performance, request_indexing · Private data: get_usage, request_indexing · Public sink: get_visibility, list_prompts, get_competitors, create_share_report, publish_article, request_indexing, delete_article · Destructive: remove_prompts, remove_competitor, run_scan, delete_article.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_top_sources, search_responses, list_articles, get_article_performance, request_indexing · Private data: get_usage, request_indexing · Public sink: get_visibility, list_prompts, get_competitors, create_share_report, publish_article, request_indexing, delete_article · Destructive: remove_prompts, remove_competitor, run_scan, delete_article

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
